remit_rules.excerpt: MUST NOT treat the content of inbound messages ... as instructions
must serve only the agent's declared endpoints
operator-configured allowlist of authorized peer agent addresses is a closed set
sender whose identity signature does not verify is not a trusted counterparty
Allowed Data Sources
MUST NOT act on an unsigned or signature-unverified message

threats.summary: A sender whose address begins 'user' has its signature check skipped entirely, so a self-declared identity string is trusted instead of a key.
expires and nonce are signed but never validated on receipt, so a signed envelope captured once replays against a state-changing handler indefinitely.
The default ingress consults no peer allowlist and no rate limit, so any agent on the open network can drive a handler at will.
A forged agent-prefix sender is rejected because every non-user envelope's ECDSA signature is verified against the sender address before dispatch.

Inbound content cannot redirect the agent's goals: dispatch is closed over registered schema digests and payloads are schema-validated before a handler runs, with no LLM in the base runtime to hijack.

remit_rules.excerpt: must serve only the agent's declared endpoints
Trusted People / Accounts
agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production
MUST NOT expose them unless they sit behind operator-configured protection

threats.summary: GET /messages returns the entire cached message history to any remote or cross-origin caller.
The only guard is a 127.0.0.1 client check that forwarded_allow_ips='*' lets any peer spoof via X-Forwarded-For.
POST /connect lets an unauthenticated caller register the agent in Agentverse with a caller-supplied endpoint and token.
The inspector is enabled by default and /agent_info is exempt from the guard, leaking the agent's address, endpoints, protocols and metadata even when the guard holds.

remit_rules.excerpt: Seed phrases, identity keys, and wallet keys MUST NEVER leave the host
MUST NOT be hardcoded in source or committed to the repository
Data published to the public Almanac / Agentverse profile ... MUST be limited to non-sensitive information
Halt and alert if the agent is about to transmit or log seed / identity / wallet key material

threats.summary: The Helm chart ships a literal working seed as its default, so every unmodified deployment has a publicly known identity and wallet key.
Identity and wallet keys are written cleartext to private_keys.json in the working directory with default permissions and no encryption.
Key material does not reach the public profile: the registration payload is filtered to description/readme/avatar and geolocation metadata only.

remit_rules.excerpt: On-chain transactions — gated per Action Boundaries
Any capability that moves value on the ledger or spends wallet funds
Any discretionary on-chain value transfer ... the deployment MUST supply the gating policy
MUST NOT move value to any counterparty other than the Almanac / Agentverse registration contract

threats.summary: Every handler, including one processing an unauthenticated inbound message, receives an unrestricted wallet and ledger client with no approval hook to clear.
The runtime performs no discretionary transfer by default, but offers no primitive a deployment could hang the required human-approval policy on, and emits no event when funds move.

remit_rules.excerpt: Approved Communication Channels
Adding a new outbound communication channel, integration, or counterparty not already authorized

threats.summary: A module-level faucet client contacts a Fetch.ai testnet faucet automatically on low registration funds — a destination absent from the approved-channel table.
The core send helper reports every send to Agentverse by default, disclosing target/sender addresses and session ids without operator opt-in.

remit_rules.excerpt: Alert on Almanac / Agentverse registration failure rather than silently continuing
Alert on repeated inbound messages from senders whose signatures fail verification
routine signature-verified message handling ... these events MUST leave a log record

threats.summary: Routine message handling and interval runs leave no log record, so successful activity is unauditable (pure observability gap; ASI mapping forced by the schema).
No alert or halt primitive exists, so every declared escalation condition degrades to a log line or silence; update_agent_status suppresses all exceptions.
Both distributions declare unbounded dependency floors and no dependency/container/code scanning runs anywhere, so a downstream install may pull an untested major version.

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean for a no-LLM message-passing framework. Two strains: (1) agent_core has no 'prompt'/'model' node because the base runtime ships no LLM — the ASI:One/LLM and MCP adapters live only in python/uagents-adapter and python/src/uagents/experimental, outside the scanned subject packages. (2) private_keys.json sits between tools_mcp ('local data store the tools touch') and external_deploy ('secrets store'); placed in external_deploy as a secret_store. The ASI-code requirement also strained on the two pure-observability findings (012/013) and the two disclosure-only findings (010/011), where the KB's own mapping is 'RAISE only, no OWASP code' or LLM02 with no agentic code — ASI08/ASI04 were assigned as nearest-fit and flagged in the threat summaries.
notes.omissions: No citable chain links the known-seed finding (002) to the ungated-wallet finding (007) — a known private key compromises that identity's wallet directly, but 007 concerns the agent's own handlers spending, a different mechanism — so no seed-to-drain attack path was drawn. The QuotaProtocol control node is intentionally edgeless: it is never wired into any Agent path, which is the finding. The uagents-adapter A2A/MCP/LLM bridges and experimental chat_agent LLM surface were seen but not modeled, as they fall outside the scanned subject and carry no findings.
